mainTopic: Does worshipping a stalk of wheat forbid its flour for the altar? Comparing it to a pregnant animal used for bestiality, then rejecting that comparison. A new question follows: may a לולב be taken from a worshipped palm tree?
overview: The amud opens by finishing a comparison: wheat stalks someone bowed to are like an animal that was already pregnant when it was used for bestiality, so the flour should be forbidden for מנחות. The גמרא rejects this, because a fetus stays an animal while wheat turns into flour, a new form. ריש לקיש then asks whether a לולב from a worshipped palm tree may be used for the מצוה. רב דימי reports the question differently, as asking whether something pushed away from a מצוה stays pushed away. A proof from covering blood (אין דיחוי אצל מצות) is rejected, and the question ends in תיקו. רב פפא asks whether parts of a worshipped animal may be used for תכלת or for the instruments of the מקדש. That question also ends in תיקו, according to the view that the main song is with the mouth. רבה asks whether water from a privately owned spring someone bowed to may be used for נסכים. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a fallen wall next to a house of עבודה זרה may not be rebuilt in place, and it begins the case of a jointly owned wall.

steps.title: Pregnant first, then bestiality: everyone forbids, and wheat is the same
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the comparison was that the dispute is only when the bestiality came before the pregnancy. Here the גמרא finishes it: if the animal was already pregnant, everyone forbids the offspring, and the worshipped wheat is like that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the animals became pregnant first and only later were used for bestiality, everyone agrees the offspring are forbidden. Here too, the wheat case is like 'pregnant first, then bestiality.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a comparison. Wheat kernels already inside a stalk someone bowed to are like a fetus already inside an animal used for bestiality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that was נרבע is disqualified for the altar. Its offspring are disputed only when the pregnancy came after the act. If the fetus was already there during the act, it was 'part of' the act, so everyone forbids it. The kernels were already in the stalk when it was worshipped, so the flour should be forbidden for מנחות too.

keyTerms.meaning: They were used for bestiality, which disqualifies them for the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The order matters. 'Bestiality, then pregnant' is the disputed case. 'Pregnant, then bestiality' is the case everyone forbids. The wheat is being compared to the second one.

phrases.english: But if they became pregnant and later were used for bestiality,
all agree they (the offspring) are forbidden,
and here too,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the wheat stalk someone bowed to, the case the גמרא was asking about.

phrases.english: it is like 'they became pregnant and later were used for bestiality.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא נָמֵי כְּעִיבְּרוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף נִרְבְּעוּ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison begun just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The flour of worshipped wheat stalks is forbidden for מנחות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that offspring are forbidden by everyone when the pregnancy came before the bestiality.

steps.title: A second version of the same comparison
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the tradition states the full idea in one piece. The dispute is only when bestiality came first. When the pregnancy came first, everyone forbids, and the wheat stalks are like that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: the dispute is when they were used for bestiality and only later became pregnant. But if they became pregnant first and later were used for bestiality, everyone agrees it is forbidden. These stalks too are like 'pregnant first, then bestiality.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of how this comparison was said. The reasoning is the same: the wheat is like the 'pregnant first' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The content barely changes. The dispute is limited to 'bestiality, then pregnant', and the 'pregnant, then bestiality' case is forbidden by everyone. The wheat stalks are again placed in the forbidden case.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
The dispute is when they were used for bestiality and later became pregnant,
but if they became pregnant and later were used for bestiality,
all agree it is forbidden,
and these too
phrases.notes: 'These' are the wheat stalks someone bowed to.

phrases.english: are like 'they became pregnant and later were used for bestiality.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the same comparison.
steps.raayaObject: The flour of worshipped wheat stalks is forbidden for מנחות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of 'pregnant first, then bestiality'.

steps.title: The comparison fails: a fetus stays an animal, but wheat becomes flour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. The fetus was an animal at the start and is still an animal now; it was just behind a closed 'door'. Wheat, though, started as kernels and is now flour, a changed form.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, it was an animal at the start and it is an animal now. It is just that a door was shut in front of it. Here, it was wheat at the start and now it is flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the comparison from the last two steps. It shows the animal case and the wheat case are really different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fetus is a full animal all along; the womb only hid it like a closed door. So it truly took part in the forbidden act. Flour is a new form that did not exist when the stalk was worshipped. So the animal case gives no proof about the flour, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejecting a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: No proof from the animal case. A fetus does not change its identity, but wheat that becomes flour does. So the question about flour from worshipped wheat is left unanswered.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a change in form (wheat to flour) can matter for whether something counts as the same object that was worshipped.

phrases.english: How can you compare?
There, it was an animal at the start
and now it is an animal;
it is just a door that was shut in front of it.
phrases.notes: The 'door' is the womb. The fetus was a whole animal all along, just hidden behind it.

phrases.english: Here, at the start it was wheat
and now it is flour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in both versions.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the 'pregnant first, then bestiality' case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A fetus keeps its identity as an animal, but wheat changes into flour, a new form.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks about a לולב from a worshipped palm tree
steps.stepSummary: A new question begins. If someone bowed to a palm tree, may its לולב be used for the מצוה of לולב?
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש asked: if someone bowed down to a palm tree, what is the law about using its לולב for the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. ריש לקיש asks whether a לולב from a worshipped palm tree may be used for the מצוה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the wheat question, this asks whether something connected to an object that was worshipped can be used for a holy purpose. Here the purpose is a מצוה instead of the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question (a real question, not an attack)
The palm branch taken on סוכות

phrases.english: Reish Lakish asked:
One who bows down to a palm tree,
what is the law about its lulav for the מצוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related question after the wheat discussion ends without a proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a לולב from a palm tree someone bowed to may be used for the מצוה.

steps.title: Narrowing the question to a tree worshipped after planting
steps.stepSummary: The question does not apply to a tree planted for idol worship, which is forbidden even for ordinary use. It applies to a tree planted normally and worshipped later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't ask about a tree planted from the start for idol worship, because it is forbidden even for ordinary use. Ask about a tree planted normally and worshipped later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is sharpening the question from step 4 by setting aside the case where the answer is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree planted for idol worship is fully forbidden, so its לולב is surely unusable for a מצוה. The real question only exists for a tree that was planted normally and worshipped afterward.

phrases.english: With a tree that one planted from the start for this purpose
phrases.notes: "For this purpose" means planted in order to be worshipped.

phrases.english: do not ask the question,
since even for ordinary use it is forbidden.
When should you ask it?
With a tree that one planted and only later worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the question asked in step 4 to one specific case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of worshipped tree the לולב question is really about.

steps.title: According to the רבנן, is the לולב too disgusting for a מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה forbids even ordinary use of such a tree, so the question only applies according to the רבנן. Even if ordinary use is allowed, is it disgusting to use for a מצוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't ask according to רבי יוסי בר יהודה, since he forbids even ordinary use. Ask according to the רבנן: for a מצוה, what is the law? Is it disgusting to use for Heaven, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question further and then states exactly what it is asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that a tree planted and then worshipped is not forbidden. Even so, a מצוה is service of Heaven and might need a higher standard. The question is whether something tied to idol worship is too disgusting (מאיס) for that.

keyTerms.meaning: Toward the Most High, for use in serving Heaven

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda
phrases.notes: Earlier in the מסכת (on 45b) he held that a tree planted and later worshipped becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: do not ask the question,
since even for ordinary use it is forbidden.
Ask it according to the Rabbis,
regarding a מצוה, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי מְאִיס כְּלַפֵּי גָּבוֹהַּ אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Is it disgusting toward the Most High, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the question by opinion and states the exact issue.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether something allowed for ordinary use is still too disgusting to use for a מצוה because it was worshipped.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a מצוה object may need a higher standard than mere permission to use it.

steps.title: רב דימי's version: does once-unfit mean always unfit?
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that the question was about an אשירה whose idol status was cancelled. Does something pushed away from a מצוה stay pushed away?
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: the question was about an אשירה that was cancelled. Is there permanent pushing-away for מצוות, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a different version of what the question really was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the tree was an idol, its לולב could not be used. After the idol status was cancelled, the question is whether it becomes fit again or stays unfit forever. That is the idea of דחוי: once pushed off, always pushed off.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
A tree that is worshipped as an idol
Being pushed off: once unfit, staying unfit

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
He was asking about an ashera whose idol status was cancelled,
phrases.notes: "He" is the one who first asked the question about the palm tree.

phrases.english: is there being pushed off for מצוות
or is there no being pushed off for מצוות?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the 'disgusting' version of the question with a different one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an object that became unfit for a מצוה can become fit again.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same question as step 6. Step 6 asks whether it is disgusting. רב דימי asks whether something once unfit stays unfit forever.

steps.title: Trying to answer from covering the blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about covering blood: if a person covered it and it became uncovered, he is exempt; if the wind covered it, he must cover it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Answer it from what we learned: if he covered it and it became uncovered, he is exempt from covering again. If the wind covered it, he is obligated to cover it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof for רב דימי's question. It brings a משנה that will be used in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of the wind is the important one: the blood was covered, so the obligation seemed to disappear, yet he still must cover it. This will be used to test whether a מצוה that was pushed off can come back.

keyTerms.meaning: From what we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Resolve it from what we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in חולין about covering the blood of a slaughtered wild animal or bird.

phrases.english: If he covered it and it became uncovered, he is exempt from covering,
if the wind covered it, he is obligated to cover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an attempt to answer רב דימי's question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether there is דחוי by מצוות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן explains the wind case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the wind case requires covering only if the blood became uncovered again. If it stayed covered, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the משנה only taught this when it became uncovered again. But if it did not become uncovered again, he is exempt from covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה. This finishes setting up the proof, which the גמרא will use next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the wind covered the blood, the obligation was pushed off for a while. Once it became uncovered again, the obligation came back. That looks like a case where being pushed off was not permanent.
steps.whyThisMatters: This case is the material the גמרא will use to decide whether something pushed off from a מצוה can return.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They taught this only when it then became uncovered again,
phrases.notes: "This" is the wind case, where he must cover the blood.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא חָזַר וְנִתְגַּלָּה — פָּטוּר מִלְּכַסּוֹת.
phrases.english: but if it did not become uncovered again, he is exempt from covering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה cited in step 8 to build the proof.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a pushed-off obligation can return.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's reading of the wind case in the משנה of כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: Why must he cover the blood again once it was already pushed away?
steps.stepSummary: Inside the quoted discussion, the גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: once the wind covered the blood and he was exempt, why should it matter that it became uncovered again?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: when the blood became uncovered again, what difference does that make? Since it was pushed away, it should stay pushed away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the earlier discussion about covering blood. Here it raises a challenge against רבי יוחנן's ruling, and this sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the wind covered the blood, the obligation to cover it was 'pushed away.' The challenge argues that a pushed-away obligation should never come back, even if the blood is later uncovered. That is exactly our question about the אשירה, so the answer will matter for us.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (an earlier discussion is being quoted)
Since it was pushed away, it stays pushed away

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
phrases.notes: This is an earlier discussion of רבי יוחנן's ruling about blood the wind covered (step 9).

phrases.english: When it then became uncovered again, what of it?
Since it was pushed away, it is pushed away!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בָּהּ: כִּי חָזַר וְנִתְגַּלָּה מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's statement in step 9 within the quoted discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that blood covered by the wind must be covered again if it became uncovered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the wind covering exempted him, the obligation was pushed away, and pushed-away obligations should not return.

steps.title: רב פפא: there is no pushing away with מצות
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the blood case teaches אין דיחוי אצל מצות. Once the reason for the exemption is gone, the מצוה comes back. This seems to answer our question about the אשירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: This teaches that there is no 'pushing away' when it comes to מצות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge and draws a general rule from רבי יוחנן's ruling. This finishes the proof the גמרא started in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing is ever permanently pushed away from a מצוה, then the cancelled אשירה should also become fit again for a מצוה. So the question from step 7 seems solved.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches / this shows (a rule drawn from an earlier source)
There is no permanent pushing away with מצות

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key rule the whole question depends on. If it applies in every case, the cancelled אשירה can be used for a מצוה.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said,
This is to say:
There is no pushing away with regard to מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10, which completes the proof for the question of step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The question of step 7: does something pushed away from a מצוה stay pushed away?
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling on blood covered by the wind, as explained by רב פפא: אין דיחוי אצל מצות.

steps.title: The question was about רב פפא's rule itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The question was really whether רב פפא's rule applies even to be lenient, or whether he was unsure and only uses it to be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question was asked about רב פפא's own rule. Was it clear to רב פפא that there is no pushing away with מצות, whether that leads to a leniency or to a stringency? Or perhaps he was unsure, so we use the rule to be strict but not to be lenient?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the original question was never about whether רב פפא's rule exists. It was about how far the rule goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the blood case the rule makes things stricter, because he must cover the blood again. In the אשירה case it would make things more lenient, because the לולב would be allowed for a מצוה. If רב פפא was really unsure, he would only rule strictly, so the blood case proves nothing about the אשירה.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt about it

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not reject רב פפא's rule. It only says we don't know whether he held it for sure, or only out of doubt, which would mean using it to be strict and never to be lenient.

phrases.english: For it was about Rav Pappa's rule itself that he asked,
phrases.notes: 'He' is ריש לקיש, who asked the original question about the אשירה.

phrases.english: Is it clear to Rav Pappa
that there is no pushing away with regard to מצוות,
no difference whether it leads to leniency
phrases.notes: Leniency is the אשירה case, where the rule would let you use the לולב for a מצוה.

phrases.english: and no difference whether it leads to stringency?
phrases.notes: Stringency is the blood case, where the rule makes him cover the blood again.

phrases.english: Or perhaps he is unsure about it,
and to be strict we say it,
but to be lenient we do not say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the blood case is rejected. רב פפא's rule itself is not rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The blood case only uses the rule to be strict. If רב פפא held the rule only out of doubt, it cannot be used to be lenient in the אשירה case.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו. We do not know whether a cancelled אשירה is fit for a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the question stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it cannot settle the question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the only proof was rejected, there is no source that decides whether אין דיחוי אצל מצות applies to be lenient. So the question of the cancelled אשירה stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: The blood case shows that a מצוה can come back after being pushed away (אין דיחוי אצל מצות). We still don't know whether this rule can be used to be lenient, like using a לולב from a cancelled אשירה. The question ends in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion after the proof was rejected in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of whether a cancelled אשירה, which was pushed away from a מצוה, may now be used for a מצוה is left unresolved.

steps.title: Can wool from a worshipped animal be used for תכלת?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether the wool of an animal that someone bowed down to may be used for תכלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If someone bowed down to an animal, may its wool be used for תכלת?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רב פפא asks whether wool from an animal that was worshipped can be used for the blue תכלת wool.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal was bowed to, which gives it a problem of עבודה זרה. The wool is a part of that animal that can be cut off and used. רב פפא wants to know if that wool is still fit for a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked / raised a question he did not know the answer to
Sky-blue wool used for a מצוה

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
One who bows down to an animal,
what is the law of its wool for תכלת?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether that wool may be dyed blue and used for the מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The אשירה question ended in תיקו in step 13; now a new question about a worshipped animal begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the wool of a worshipped animal may be used for תכלת.

steps.title: This question was already asked by others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תכלת רב פפא means, and shows that either way his question repeats an earlier one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which תכלת is he talking about? If he means the תכלת for the כהנים' clothing, that is the same as רמי בר חמא's question. If he means the תכלת for ציצית, that is the same as ריש לקיש's question.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's question. Whichever kind of תכלת he means, someone already asked that question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תכלת for the כהנים' clothing is a use in the מקדש, which matches רמי בר חמא's question about worshipped items used for holy service. תכלת for ציצית is a regular מצוה, which matches ריש לקיש's question about a לולב from a worshipped palm tree. So why ask it again?

phrases.english: תכלת for what?
If it is תכלת for the כהנים,
phrases.notes: This means the blue wool woven into the כהנים' special clothing.

phrases.english: that is the same as the question of Rami bar Chama,
and if it is תכלת for ציצית,
that is the same as the question of Reish Lakish!
phrases.notes: That is his question about a לולב taken from a palm tree that was worshipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב פפא's question in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's question about wool for תכלת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible meanings of תכלת were already covered by earlier questions, so the question adds nothing new.

steps.title: He asked it because of other uses of the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees the wool question was not needed, but says רב פפא included it as part of a list of new questions about other body parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it is true that he did not need to ask it. He asked it because there are other things he wanted to ask: Its wool, may it be used for תכלת? Its horns, may they be used for trumpets? Its thigh bones, may they be used for flutes? Its innards, may they be used for harp strings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the wool question really was not needed. רב פפא only mentioned it as the start of a list of new questions about the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new questions are about musical instruments: horns for trumpets, bones for flutes, innards for strings. These were not covered by רמי בר חמא or ריש לקיש. The wool was just listed together with them.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא says רב פפא's wool question was wrong. It admits the wool part was already asked, and explains that the real new questions are the other body parts.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so
that he did not need to ask it,
and the reason he does ask it
is because there are other matters:
Its wool, what is its law for תכלת?
Its horns, what is their law for trumpets?
Its thigh bones, what is their law for flutes?
Its innards, what is their law for harp strings?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא הֲוָה לְמִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees with the challenge but reframes the question as part of a larger new list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's question seemed to be only about wool, which was already asked.
steps.terutzMaskana: The real new questions are about horns, thigh bones, and innards used for musical instruments; the wool was just listed with them.

steps.title: If instruments are the main song, it is surely forbidden
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that the main song in the מקדש is the instruments, the animal parts are definitely forbidden, so there is no question.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the main part of the song is the instruments, you have no question. It is surely forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to narrow down רב פפא's question. According to one view about the music in the מקדש, the answer is clear: forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the instruments are the main part of the song, then the instruments are part of the service of the offering. A worshipped animal may not be used for an offering, so its parts may not be used for those instruments either. This suggests רב פפא's question can only be asked according to the other view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
The main part of the song is with instruments
You do not need to ask

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the answer depends on a basic argument about the song in the מקדש: whether the instruments or the singing is the main part.

phrases.english: According to the one who says:
The main part of the song is with instruments,
phrases.notes: He means the song the לויים performed in the מקדש while the offerings were brought.

phrases.english: you have no question,
for it is surely forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר עִיקַּר שִׁירָה בִּכְלִי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the new questions from step 16 by settling them according to one view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether parts of a worshipped animal may be used for musical instruments in the מקדש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to the view that the main song is the instruments, it is definitely forbidden.

steps.title: The question only works if the main song is with the mouth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains when רב פפא's question about instruments made from the animal really applies. It applies according to the view that the main song is with the mouth, so the instruments only sweeten the sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: When should you ask it? According to the one who says the main song is with the mouth, the instruments are only there to sweeten the sound. So may we bring them, or perhaps even so they are forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 17 showed there is no question according to the view that instruments are the main song. Now the גמרא shows where the question does apply: the view that the main song is sung with the mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the instruments are only extras that make the singing sound nicer, maybe it is fine to use ones made from a worshipped animal. Or maybe it is still not proper to use such things in the עבודה. The question is now clearly framed.

keyTerms.meaning: The main song in the מקדש is the singing with the mouth
To sweeten the sound, only adding to the singing
According to the one who says

phrases.english: When should you ask the question?
According to the one who says:
the main song is with the mouth,
the instruments are merely to sweeten the sound,
so we may bring them,
or perhaps even so it is forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 17 removed the question under one view, this step places it under the other view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If instruments only add to the singing, may ones made from a worshipped animal be used?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question about the instruments ends without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this question with תיקו. No answer is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We still don't know if instruments from a worshipped animal may be used, according to the view that the main song is with the mouth. This closes רב פפא's set of questions.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: According to the view that the instruments are the main song, they are surely forbidden. According to the view that the mouth is the main song, it is a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question raised in step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Unresolved whether instruments from a worshipped animal may be used when they only add to the singing.

steps.title: Water from a spring someone bowed to
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks whether water from a spring that someone bowed down to may be used for נסכים on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked: If someone bows down to a spring, what is the law about using its water for נסכים?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question starts here. רבה asks whether a spring's water can be poured on the מזבח after someone worshipped the spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier questions about things that were worshipped, this asks if worship makes the item unfit for a מצוה in the מקדש. Here the item is flowing water.

keyTerms.meaning: One who bows down, as worship

phrases.english: רבה asked:
One who bows down to a spring,
what is the law about its water for libations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question in the same series about worshipped items used for a מצוה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is water from a worshipped spring fit for נסכים?

steps.title: What exactly is רבה unsure about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבה is unsure whether the person bowed to his own reflection or to the water. It rejects this, because then he could ask the same question about a simple bucket of water for everyday use.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he unsure about? If you say: is he bowing to his reflection, or to the water? Then he should ask about a bucket of water for ordinary use!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the real doubt is. It tests one possible reading of רבה's question and pushes back against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the doubt were whether he bowed to his reflection, it would apply to any water, even a bucket used for everyday purposes. There would be no reason to ask only about a spring and about נסכים, so this cannot be the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Reflection, the image seen in the water
Ordinary, everyday use, not for the מקדש

phrases.english: What is he asking?
If you say: is he bowing to his reflection,
or perhaps is he bowing to the water?
Then let him ask about a bucket for ordinary use!
phrases.notes: Meaning: that doubt would come up even with plain bucket water, so why mention a spring and the מזבח?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to define the doubt in step 20 and challenges that definition.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבה's question as reflection versus water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That doubt would apply to any water, even for everyday use, so the specific case of a spring and נסכים would make no sense.

steps.title: He bowed to the water, but which water?
steps.stepSummary: He certainly bowed to the water. The doubt is whether he bowed to the water in front of him, which has already flowed away, or to the flow of the spring as a whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he bows to the water, and this is the question: Is he bowing to the water in front of him, and that first water has already gone away? Or perhaps he bows to the flow of the water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real doubt. It is about flowing water, which explains why רבה asked about a spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water that was there when he bowed has flowed away, so the water we take now is new. If he bowed only to that water, the new water is fine. If he bowed to the ongoing flow, all of the spring's water would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Really. Used to start an answer that keeps the basic idea
The first waters have already gone
The flow, or stream, of the water

phrases.english: Really, he is bowing to the water,
and this is what he is asking:
Is he bowing to the water in front of him,
and the first waters have already gone away,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא לְדַבְרוּנָא דְּמַיָּא קָא סָגֵיד?
phrases.english: or perhaps he is bowing to the flow of the water?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לְמַיָּא קָא סָגֵיד, וְהָכִי קָמִבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21 by giving a doubt that only fits a flowing spring.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubt was whether he bowed to his reflection or to the water.
steps.terutzMaskana: He bowed to the water. The doubt is whether he bowed to the water present then or to the ongoing flow.

steps.title: But public water cannot become forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the question using רבי יוחנן's rule, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, that water belonging to the public cannot become forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it even become forbidden? Didn't רבי יוחנן say in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: Water of the public cannot become forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the question itself. A spring usually belongs to everyone, so worship by one person should not forbid it at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot forbid something that is not his. If springs are public water, there is nothing to ask, either way.

phrases.english: But do they even become forbidden?
But didn't רבי יוחנן say
in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק:
Water of the public does not become forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מִיתַּסְרִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question in step 22 can come up at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The basic idea that a spring's water can become forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Public water cannot become forbidden through one person's worship, so the question has no case.

steps.title: A spring coming up on private land
steps.stepSummary: The question is about a spring that comes up from the ground in one person's own property, so it is not public water.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a spring that comes up from the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. רבה is talking about a spring that comes up in a private place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule covers public water, like a river that flows past everyone. A spring that comes up out of the ground on someone's own land belongs to him, so his worship could forbid it, and רבה's question stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for a certain case

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's question is about a privately owned spring. Did the worship forbid only the water present at the time, which has flowed away, or the whole flow?

phrases.english: It is only needed
where the water comes up from the ground.
phrases.notes: He means a spring that comes up on someone's own land, so it isn't public water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by limiting the case to a privately owned spring.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The spring is public water and cannot become forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about a spring coming up from the ground in a private place, which can become forbidden.

steps.title: A fallen wall next to a house of idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a wall between a person's house and a house of עבודה זרה that fell may not be rebuilt in place. He must move four אמות into his own property and build there.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone's house was right next to a house of idol worship and the wall fell, he may not rebuild it. So what should he do? He pulls back four אמות into his own land and builds the wall there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a practical case. A person's wall next to a house of עבודה זרה fell down, and the משנה tells him he may not rebuild it in the same spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rebuilding the wall in its old place would also give the house of עבודה זרה back its wall, so that is forbidden. The משנה does not leave him stuck. It gives a solution: build the wall four אמות back, inside his own property.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of a new משנה.
Idol worship. Here it means a building used for idol worship.
He pulls in, he moves back inward.

steps.confusionAlert: He is not forbidden to rebuild his house at all. He is only forbidden to rebuild the wall in the same spot. Moving four אמות into his own land solves the problem.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the topic of the next lines: how a Jew deals with property that touches a house of עבודה זרה without helping it.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One whose house was
adjacent to a house of idol worship,
and it fell —
phrases.notes: "It" means the dividing wall between his house and the house of idol worship.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to rebuild it.
What should he do?
He withdraws four cubits into his own property
and builds.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁהָיָה בֵּיתוֹ סָמוּךְ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא finished discussing the spring someone bowed to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fallen wall next to a house of עבודה זרה may not be rebuilt in place. The owner must pull back four אמות into his own property and build there.

steps.title: Opening the case of a shared wall
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new case: a wall that belongs partly to the person and partly to the עבודה זרה. The ruling comes in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the wall belonged to him and to the house of idol worship together —
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next case, a wall shared between him and the house of עבודה זרה. The ruling for this case continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 was about a wall next to the house of עבודה זרה. Now the משנה asks about a wall that is jointly owned by both sides. Ownership will affect how the wall is measured and handled.

phrases.english: If it belonged to him and to the house of idol worship —
phrases.notes: The משנה is talking about the wall between them. What happens in this case comes in the next lines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case to the משנה's rule about the fallen wall: a wall owned jointly by him and the עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This line only sets up the case of a jointly owned wall. The ruling follows in the continuation.
